description: Rungs where closurec's output differs from the pinned oracle. Each entry pins the current closurec output so the gap cannot silently widen, and so closing it fails the harness — which is the signal to delete the entry.

ladder_t3_function_expr_advanced.reason: closurec does not propagate a single-use function expression to its call site and eliminate the binding.

ladder_t3_iife_advanced.reason: closurec does not inline an immediately invoked function expression.

ladder_t3_nested_fn_advanced.reason: closurec does not inline a single-use nested function. `inline` is registered only under ADVANCED, and even there handles a narrower case than upstream.

ladder_t3_nested_fn_simple.reason: closurec does not inline a single-use nested function. `inline` is registered only under ADVANCED, and even there handles a narrower case than upstream.

ladder_t3_unused_local_advanced.reason: closurec does not remove a function-local binding that is never read. `remove-unused-vars` is gated to ADVANCED, but upstream removes scope-local bindings at SIMPLE too, where the open-world contract does not apply.

ladder_t3_unused_local_simple.reason: closurec does not remove a function-local binding that is never read. `remove-unused-vars` is gated to ADVANCED, but upstream removes scope-local bindings at SIMPLE too, where the open-world contract does not apply.

ladder_t4_for_loop_advanced.reason: closurec does not rename loop-header locals. Upstream renames `i` to `a`. This is the CCR-022 renaming-breadth gap.

ladder_t4_if_else_advanced.reason: closurec does not propagate a known binding into the condition, so the branch survives as a ternary instead of collapsing. Upstream folds it away entirely. This is the CCR-068 value-propagation gap.

ladder_t4_if_else_simple.reason: closurec does not propagate a known binding into the condition, so the branch survives as a ternary instead of collapsing. Upstream folds it away entirely. This is the CCR-068 value-propagation gap.

ladder_t4_switch_advanced.reason: Upstream propagates the scrutinee `x = 1`, selects the live case and discards the rest of the switch, leaving only its effect. closurec emits the input unchanged. Single-use value propagation, CCR-068. The emitter punctuation that used to differ here is fixed (CCR-073).

ladder_t4_try_catch_advanced.reason: Upstream renames the catch parameter `e` to `a`, which closurec skips. That is CCR-022, and it is now the only difference on this rung: the missing statement terminator (CCR-073) is fixed.

ladder_t4_try_catch_simple.reason: Upstream renames the catch parameter `e` to `a`, which closurec skips. That is CCR-022, and it is now the only difference on this rung: the missing statement terminator (CCR-073) is fixed.

ladder_t4_while_advanced.reason: closurec rewrites the while into a for but leaves the initializer as a separate statement rather than hoisting it into the for header (CCR-074). The ADVANCED rung additionally needs the loop-local rename of CCR-022.

ladder_t4_while_simple.reason: closurec rewrites the while into a for but leaves the initializer as a separate statement rather than hoisting it into the for header (CCR-074). The ADVANCED rung additionally needs the loop-local rename of CCR-022.

ladder_t5_regex_advanced.reason: closurec does not propagate a single-use regular-expression literal into its use site (CCR-068).

ladder_t6_arrow_advanced.reason: closurec does not propagate a single-use value or function into its use site and eliminate the binding; upstream reduces the program to its observable effect. This is the CCR-068 value-propagation gap.

ladder_t6_block_scope_advanced.reason: closurec keeps the block and the binding. Upstream propagates the value, drops the dead binding, and unwraps the now-single-statement block, leaving `console.log(2);`. Two causes: the local-scope propagation gap (CCR-078) and brace-dropping (CCR-076).

ladder_t6_block_scope_simple.reason: closurec keeps the block and the binding. Upstream propagates the value, drops the dead binding, and unwraps the now-single-statement block, leaving `console.log(2);`. Two causes: the local-scope propagation gap (CCR-078) and brace-dropping (CCR-076).

ladder_t6_class_advanced.reason: closurec refuses valid JavaScript that upstream compiles: a class method following a constructor fails at the parse stage. This is a front-end capability gap, not an optimizer one. Note it fails only on the typed path — WHITESPACE_ONLY passes, because that path never parses.

ladder_t6_for_of_advanced.reason: Three differences remain: upstream rewrites `const` to `let`, renames the loop binding (CCR-022), and drops the braces around the single-statement body (CCR-076), which also removes the space before `[`. The statement terminator now matches (CCR-073).

ladder_t6_let_const_advanced.reason: At SIMPLE this runs the OPPOSITE way to every other rung: closurec propagates the const into its use site and upstream does not, so we optimize MORE than the oracle. That may be a win or an unsound propagation — tracked as CCR-078. At ADVANCED the ordinary CCR-068 gap applies.

ladder_t6_local_const_advanced.reason: closurec does not propagate a binding declared inside a function. `inline-variables` considers only TOP-LEVEL `const` declarations, so a function-local one is never substituted and the body cannot fold. Upstream folds `b+1` to `3` at SIMPLE and inlines the whole call at ADVANCED. CCR-078.

ladder_t6_local_let_advanced.reason: Same gap as `local_const`, and it shows the constraint is scope, not `const`-ness: a function-local binding is not observable from outside, so upstream folds `let` here as readily as `const`. `inline-variables` takes only top-level `const`, so neither is reached. CCR-078.
